chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa from 'Ali ibn Sayf from his brother al-Husayn from his father Sayf ibn 'Amira from 'Amr ibn Shimr from Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him). He said:
Whoever loses children and counts them for the sake of Allah, they will shield him from the Fire by the permission of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

key_terms.حجبوه: hajabahu — they will shield or veil him, forming a barrier between him and the Fire
key_terms.قدّم: qaddama — to send forth, meaning children who precede a parent in death
key_terms.يحتسبهم: yahtasibuhum — counts them for reward with Allah, meaning to accept their loss with patience and seek divine recompense

ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about the reward of parents who lose children?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) offers consolation to parents who have experienced the death of their children. The word 'qaddama' (sends forth) implies that the children precede the parent in death. The key condition is 'ihtisab' — accepting the loss with patience and seeking divine reward rather than despairing. The promise that the deceased children will act as a 'barrier' (hajaba) from Hellfire reflects the broader Islamic ethic that the righteous suffering of this world carries immense weight in the Hereafter.
